id_and_class.theory_title: Sri Ramana’s Self as Pure Consciousness
id_and_class.summary: Sri Ramana Maharshi, as explained by Michael James, teaches that the only real consciousness is intransitive awareness: awareness of nothing but its own being, ‘I am’. Awareness of objects is a fleeting semblance that borrows its existence and light from this pure awareness, so the way to know consciousness is to turn attention inward on oneself until awareness of everything else ceases.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness in its real form is pure intransitive awareness (sat-cit), consciousness that is itself pure being. It is the one real substance from which everything else derives its seeming existence, as gold ornaments derive theirs from gold.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Neither mind nor body is real. The ego, the knowing element of the mind, appears in waking and dream and vanishes in sleep, and the body and world seem to exist only in the ego's view.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (pure awareness is the sole permanent reality; transitive awareness of objects is a secondary appearance of it)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentionality belongs to transitive awareness (cidābhāsa), a semblance of consciousness directed at things that only seem to exist, like objects in a dream. The real subject knows itself by being itself, not by any act of knowing.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: All phenomena, mental or seemingly physical, are objects that appear and disappear in transitive awareness and so have no independent reality.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One infinite, indivisible, immutable being-awareness, ‘one only without a second’. Ego, mind and world are illusory appearances, like a snake seen in a rope.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Consciousness is the reality of the subject, never an object, so no objective investigation can reveal it. It is known only through self-investigation (ātma-vicāra): holding attention on the bare awareness ‘I am’.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Two forms of the one consciousness: intransitive awareness, which is real, permanent and self-shining, and transitive awareness, which is impermanent and shines with borrowed light.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-awareness, the nature of the subject, waking, dream and sleep, and liberation from mistaken identity with the body.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Only what is permanent is real. Since transitive awareness and its objects come and go, they borrow existence from pure awareness, which persists unchanged through waking, dream and sleep.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Pure awareness never changes. Transitive awareness appears whenever we take ourselves to be a body, in waking and dream, and subsides in sleep, only to return.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Pure awareness is beyond the limits of time and space and is not located anywhere.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Pure awareness is the sole reality underlying the ego, and the ego's seeming existence supports the seeming existence of all phenomena.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Multiplicity and difference seem to exist only in the ego's view. Reality is one and indivisible, so unity needs no binding.
core_claims_and_evidence: We cannot be aware of anything without being aware, but we can be aware without being aware of anything, so intransitive awareness is primary.
We experience ourselves as one body in waking, another in dream and no body in sleep, so no body can be what we are.
Stopping mental activity, as Yoga aims to do, is not enough, since it also happens in sleep and is only temporary.
Sri Ramana holds that whatever exists at one time and not another does not really exist even when it seems to.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological and contemplative: first-person analysis of waking, dream and sleep, self-investigation, and Advaita scripture.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Self-investigation (ātma-vicāra) is offered as a first-person test: attending to oneself so keenly that awareness of anything else ceases.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: James rejects the label idealism for this view, since idealisms usually take the mind to be real while Advaita treats mind and ego as illusory. This makes its place on the atlas under Idealism a matter of dispute.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The teaching says why pure awareness seems not to know itself (we mistake ourselves for a body) but not why that mistake arises in the first place.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent as radical monism: permanence is the test of reality, and only pure awareness passes it. It sits opposite modern science, which James says looks for consciousness among phenomena.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since real consciousness is the one pure awareness and any machine is a phenomenon appearing in transitive awareness, no machine can generate consciousness.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: What we actually are is permanent, unchanging awareness that is never a body, so it does not end when a body does.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The aim of life is to know ourselves as pure awareness by self-investigation, ending the false identification with body and ego.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A digital copy would preserve only phenomena and the ego's patterns, which the view treats as unreal, so nothing real would be carried over.
